subject: Sealed gatekeeper protocol and rotation Q&A
messages:
From: Danielle Park <dpark@meditech.io>

Cc: security@meditech.io
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sealed gatekeeper -- BYOK / ephemeral signer questions

Hi Sofia / Jordan,

Thanks again for walking us through the private deployment options last week. A couple of follow-ups from our security team around the BYOK story and the ephemeral signing path you mentioned:

1) We need a short annotated flow that shows where the customer-held root key (BYOK) is used versus any ephemeral signers generated in the HSM. In particular, our auditors want to understand whether the HSM ever sees unwrapped tenant keys and what the rotation outage surface looks like.

2) For compliance, we require audit evidence that an operator did not have plaintext access to the master key during rotations; sample log output would be useful.

3) Latency: our product team is worried about a signer-proxy adding >15ms p99 on token issuance paths. Any mitigations?

Can your team sketch a concise plan and call out operational guardrails (operator access, staggered rotations, telemetry) and attach any diagrams or matrices? Happy to hop on a short call to align.

Thanks,
Danielle
Security Lead, MediTech Health

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>

Hi Danielle — great questions. Posting a short design summary and next steps below, and attaching a diagram (redwood-kms-airlock-diagram.pdf). I reserved 30 min tomorrow if you want to review live.

Summary (high level):
- BYOK root key: remains off-network in customer KMS/HSM; customer-supplied root never leaves their HSM. Redwood supports an accept-only gateway for the root (wrap/unwrap operations performed by customer-side HSM).
- Sealed "gatekeeper" pattern: Redwood deploys a short-lived HSM-based ephemeral signer inside the private VPC. The ephemeral signer holds a KEK that is itself wrapped by the customer BYOK.
- Rotation behavior: KEK rotation can be automated with a two-phase commit: create ephemeral KEK, stage for X hours, switch traffic, then retire old KEK. No plaintext tenant keys are written to Redwood logs or disk.

Operational guardrails we propose:
- Staggered rotations by tenant groups (default: 3-stage rollouts over 24h).
- Operator separation: operator can trigger rotation job but cannot unwrap BYOK; unwrapping requires possession of customer HSM (remote unwrap via accept-only API).
- Audit evidence: collect signature attestations from HSM for key unwrap/creation events and ship to customer audit S3/Drive.

Latency considerations:
- For hot paths we recommend co-locating the ephemeral signer on the same subnet and using a persistent TLS session (keepalive + mTLS). That avoids per-request TLS handshakes to the signer. We include an optimization note on batching sign operations for non-real-time flows.

Next steps (recommended):
1) We’ll send the architecture diagram + rotation matrix (attached).
2) Triage any constraints from your compliance team (evidence retention windows, KMS attestation formats).
3) Quick sync (30m) to confirm rotation windows and fallback SLA.

Attaching: redwood-kms-airlock-diagram.pdf (diagram), initial rotation_matrix placeholder (will circulate XLS).

—
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Adding operational runbook points from the ops/infra side — these are the items we'll need to finalize before any production cutover: 

- Rotation matrix: exact TTL, staging window, health checks, rollback criteria. (I can provide a template).
- Telemetry: token-level signing latency histogram, success/fail counter by KEK id, unwrap attestation receipts.
- Operator access model: just-in-time sudo for rotation triggers, with MFA and ephemeral console sessions.
- Disaster recovery: pre-shared emergency unwrap procedure requiring multi-party approval and an offsite witness (documented in rotation matrix).

Operational questions for MediTech:
1) What is your maximum acceptable p99 for SMB signing flows? You mentioned ~15ms — is that a hard requirement or a guideline?
2) Can your HSM support remote-unwrap (wrap/unwrap via secure RPC) or will we need to perform an offline ceremony?

I’ll attach a short runbook template in the follow-up. If we can get answers to the two Qs, I’ll draft the detailed rotation_matrix.xlsx for your review.

—
Tessa Morgan
Principal Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference

Couple notes on performance vs safety trade-offs:
- If MediTech requires strict sub-15ms p99 on the critical path, we should consider running the ephemeral signer in a co-located hot pool (one signer per shard) to avoid network hop variability. That increases cost but keeps latency predictable.
- For most customers, a hybrid approach works: co-locate signers for the hot tier, and run a shared signer pool with aggressive caching for cold paths.
- Rotation window: propose a default of 1h staged cutover per shard with health-check gating. We should allow customers to opt for slower staged windows if they want additional audit/attestation time.

I’ve put a short internal note here: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/MT-12345 (design pointer)

Operational audit items (compliance checklist) — please review and confirm:
- Evidence: HSM-produced attestation per unwrap/create event, signed and time-stamped (retain for 1yr by default).
- Logs: KMS request/response headers (no plaintext keys), operator id, job id, and rollforward/rollback marker.
- Rotation choreography: recommend cross-checks with tenant telemetry (no error spikes for 30m post-cutover).
- Split-operator or quorum: for emergency unwrapping, require 2-of-3 operator approval plus a customer sign-off; store approvals as signed artifacts.

I will attach the rotation_matrix.xlsx (sample) after small edits — it lists staging windows and the instrumentation checks Tessa requested. Also note: we should include a minimal signed-attestation sample for MediTech compliance to validate formatting.

—
Olga Petrov
